commits.body:
Upgrades devfile gem to 0.5.2, which bumps devfile/library to v2.4.0 and
drops the vulnerable github.com/distribution/distribution/v3 dependency
containing CVE-2026-35172 and CVE-2026-33540.

devfile/library v2.4.0 changes env var ordering in generated Kubernetes
manifests (PROJECT_SOURCE now precedes PROJECTS_ROOT), so fixture files
are updated accordingly.

commits.subject: Remove potential exposure of Geo OAuth secret in Redis
commits.body:
The OAuth UID and secret were cached in Redis (L2 cache) via
the Geo multi-level cache mechanism. This left the OAuth secret
in plaintext in Redis for potential exposure for up to 2 minutes
for certain customers. This was only relevant to customers who
are still using OAuth for Geo, with Geo proxy disabled, and who's
secret was still stored in the DB in plaintext, unlike most recent
versions where it is hashed.

This fix stops caching the OAuth credentials altogether and pulls
them from the DB. The OAuth token is valid for 2 hours and no
other re-auth scenario is triggered often enough to justify caching
the OAuth credentials for Geo.

Fixes: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/594973

Changelog: security

commits.subject: Publish role-tagged traversal IDs to Knowledge Graph
commits.body:
AuthorizationContext#reporter_plus_traversal_ids now returns
`[{path, access_level}]` tuples instead of flat path strings.
Rails runs Search::GroupsFinder once per role tier (Reporter,
Developer) and keeps the stricter role on conflict, so a user
with Reporter on `1/100/` and Developer on `1/101/` ships both
paths tagged with the role they actually hold.

GKG consumes this as `claims::TraversalPathClaim` and drops
traversal paths below an entity's declared `required_role` from
the per-alias startsWith predicate, closing the aggregation-query
bypass tracked in work item 347 (the count of a Developer-gated
entity like Vulnerability grouped by a Reporter-accessible
entity like Project). See the companion GKG MR for the compiler
side of the fix.

Dead methods removed: reporter_plus_group_traversal_ids,
authorized_group_traversal_ids. Metrics (observe_traversal_ids_count,
observe_compaction_ratio, increment_threshold_exceeded,
increment_compaction_fallback) fire per tier.

commits.subject: Add namespace authorization for GitLab Duo access rules
commits.body:
Without this change, the `duo_namespace_access_rules` parameter
in the Groups API accepted any `through_namespace` ID without
verifying the caller had owner-level access to that namespace.
Although the model validation and the `build_ai_feature_rules`
`parent_id` filter prevent cross-tenant writes, there was no
explicit per-namespace authorization check at the service layer.

`Gitlab::Access::AccessDeniedError` is raised on failure, which
the Grape API layer converts to HTTP 403. Self-managed instances
are unaffected: the admin route is restricted to trusted admins.

The Groups API query-limit threshold is bumped from 101 to 103
to account for the two additional queries.

commits.subject: Fix unauthorized access via discussion resolution
commits.body:
Addresses a security vulnerability where users
could bypass note-level permissions when resolving
discussions, potentially gaining unauthorized
access to confidential/internal notes.

Changes:
- Remove duplicate can_resolve_discussion?
method from Discussion model.
- Consolidate permission checking to use
can_resolve? method.
- Update permission logic to check against
`first_note` instead of `noteable` when resolving
discussions to properly enforce note-level
permissions.
- Replace all can_resolve_discussion? calls
with can_resolve? across GraphQL types, helpers,
views, and services.
- Add security tests for confidential discussion
access control.

The fix ensures that confidential/internal notes
remain properly protected during discussion
resolution workflows while maintaining
backward compatibility.

commits.subject: Add security patch for OAuth device flow scope validation bypass
commits.body:
Add scope validation to DeviceAuthorizationRequest to prevent
privilege escalation through unauthorized scope requests.

The device authorization grant flow was not validating requested
scopes against the OAuth application's allowed scopes, allowing
attackers to request broader permissions than configured.

This patch adds proper validation until an upstream fix is available.

commits.subject: Filter LFS objects to prevent unauthorized access in merge requests
commits.body:
This commit adds validation to ensure that only LFS objects
that are legitimately linked to the source project can be linked
to the target project during a merge request.
This prevents potential unauthorized access to LFS objects
that the source project does not have permission to access.

The fix adds a new filter_valid_lfs_oids method that verifies
each LFS object ID against the source project's linked LFS
objects before allowing the link operation to proceed.

commits.subject: Always require consent for OAuth public clients
commits.body:
Require consent for every OAuth public client authentication, even if
user previously consented. This is necessary because OAuth public
clients are inherently vulnerable to client impersonation.

Vulnerability CVE-2023-34246 was fixed upstream in Doorkeeper but
remained in GitLab because GitLab overrides `new` method. This change
simply copies the upstream fix.

https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2023-34246

https://github.com/doorkeeper-gem/doorkeeper/pull/1646/commits/f202079baac4c978a01ccc9a45d78fde368ac907#diff-66fc64b17118c035403fae8265f359b94d03b14e405cf6013418c6f3c83d2817

to ghost users in MigrateRecordsToGhostUserService
and it has blocked the process of user deletion.
